body:
maria: Heads-up — ran into an edge case where sampled traces drop cost attribution because enrichment runs after sampling. We lose billing keys for a small but important subset.

derek: ugh yep seen that. Is this the late-enrich flow from edge proxies?

maria: Exactly. Edge proxy emits a tiny stub, sampler decides keep/drop, enrichment later attaches billing_key and tenant info. If dropped we can't attribute cost.

jonah: Two quick levers: 1) move sampling after enrichment (expensive), 2) attach a lightweight beacon with just billing_key pre-enrichment (cheap).

priya: We should also consider deterministic sampling based on tenant id so we never lose keys for known billable tenants.

sam: +1 for beacon. The beacon can be tiny: {"billing_key": "x", "span_id": "y"} and TTL 5s. Store in a fast KV for stitch later.

infra-bot: deploy: canary-ingest-proxy v1.3 -> deployed to us-west-2 :shipit:

maria: Beacon idea: edge sends beacon synchronously with the first span. In ingest we keep beacon records for 10s and when enrichment arrives we join on span_id. Fallback: if no beacon we try late lookup.

derek: Concern: cardinality explosion in KV if some services emit many unique billing_keys. Need eviction/compaction strategy.

jonah: We can namespace by tenant hash + minute window, compaction by LRU, and enforce max keys per-tenant. Also emit metrics for beacon creation rate.

priya: Also think about security — billing_key is sensitive. Encrypt at transport + store ephemeral only, rotate keys. KMS integration required.

sam: Implementation sketch:
```
// pseudo
emit_beacon({billing_key, span_id})
store.redis.setex("beacon:"+span_id, 10, encrypted_payload)
on_enrich(span_id) => lookup, decrypt, merge
```

maria: Nice. Let's add a validation step in enrichment: if billing_key present in beacon but enrichment logic strips it, fail closed (log + metric).

derek: For sampling: we should preserve a small deterministic sample of tenants (say 0.1%) for debugging. But for billing tenants we always force-keep via beacon + policy.

jonah: Operational questions: cost impact of beacon storage — rough calc: if 1M requests/s and beacon for 1% => 10k writes/s -> ~small Redis cluster, should be fine but need autoscaling.

priya: Can we instead include billing_key hashed into the span header so sampling can use it without storing anything? That leaks less but still sensitive if hash reversible. Use HMAC with salt.

sam: HMAC-salt approach is good: sampler checks HMAC tag instead of raw key. Enricher keeps raw after secure lookup. That reduces KV writes.

maria: Action items: 1) prod experiment with HMAC-tag approach on canary proxies (jonah + infra) 2) spike beacon fallback for tenants where HMACs fail (sam) 3) security review for transient stores + KMS (priya) 4) add observability: beacon-create-rate, beacon-hit-rate, missed-enrichments (maria).

jonah: I'll open a short RFC doc with tradeoffs and toy perf numbers. Assigning owners in that doc.

priya: I'll thread the security checklist and include key-rotation ops.

maria: Thanks — if we can get canary metrics in 48h we can decide path. :+1:

infra-bot: ticket created: P-4981 "beacon/hmac sampling experiment" assigned -> eng-platform

derek: sounds good. small note: update ingestion SLAs — stitch latency may increase slightly.

sam: ok I'll add rate-limits and eviction thresholds to the spike.

maria: cool. if anyone has other blockers speak now, otherwise syncing this into the RFC. :wave:
